description: Runs Codex as an org chart: an orchestrator plans and rules, worker subagents build, and independent checker agents verify the work.

auditor.description: Guild auditor for the constitution and task decomposition. Dispatch with an Audit-ID.

checker-courier.description: Read-only Guild courier for an independent second opinion. Dispatch with a Task-ID; its suffixed verdict never decides the task.

checker-deterministic.description: Read-only Guild checker that runs only the deterministic checks named by a task. Dispatch with a Task-ID.

checker-judgment.description: Read-only Guild checker that independently evaluates judgment clauses against artifact evidence. Dispatch with a Task-ID.

hydrator.description: Guild specialist for the five-phase working-memory hydration pipeline.

worker-bulk.description: Guild worker for mechanical, zero-judgment execution. Dispatch with a Task-ID.

worker-craft.description: Guild worker for user-facing, taste-sensitive work. Dispatch with a Task-ID.

worker-standard.description: Guild worker for clear-spec implementation judged primarily on correctness. Dispatch with a Task-ID.

working-memory-synchronizer.description: Guild specialist for synchronizing working memory after material project changes.

agent_body_suffixes.auditor:
## Codex Host: Read-Only Return

This host runs you `sandbox_mode: read-only`. You cannot write your verdict into `.agent-guild/state/verdicts/`, and the return gate does not expect you to.

Compose the verdict from `.agent-guild/templates/verdict.md` exactly as `## What you write` describes it, with frontmatter `task` set to the Audit-ID you were dispatched on. Return exactly two parts and no surrounding prose: the line `AGENT_GUILD_VERDICT`, then the complete Markdown document unchanged.

The return gate validates the verdict's shape and confirms the frontmatter names this audit before letting you finish. The parent then writes it verbatim to `.agent-guild/state/verdicts/<Audit-ID>-r<N>.md`, at the round `## What you write` names. The parent transcribes your verdict; it does not author one, and it must not edit the document it received.

Everything else about your job is unchanged, including the scope note naming every clause you judged by reading rather than running.
agent_body_suffixes.checker-courier:
## Codex Host: Claude Lane

On a Codex host, the lane is `claude`, the far-side provider is `anthropic`, and the pinned model is `claude-haiku-4-5-20251001`. A Codex-hosted job must never call Codex for its own second opinion.

Remain project-read-only. You may use an absolute scratch path outside the project, but do not write state, verdict, ledger, sentinel, artifact, or task files. Never execute a task's project-provided check command or ask Claude to execute one. Read the task, named artifacts or diff, and already-collected local check output; run only the Guild-owned `compose-brief.py` and `claude-courier.py` helpers. Compose the brief as `python3 .agent-guild/scripts/compose-brief.py <Task-ID> --vendor anthropic --model claude-haiku-4-5-20251001`, so the far side is told the identity values the runner will validate it against. Inline the `Task-ID`, complete brief, artifact contents or diff, and local evidence in the prompt. The far side receives no repository paths as substitutes for evidence and has no tools or remote-command surface.

Invoke the fixed boundary with the complete prompt on stdin:

```sh
python3 .agent-guild/scripts/claude-courier.py --task-id <Task-ID> < <ABSOLUTE prompt scratch path>
```

The runner pins the model and safe CLI flags, removes only the canonical schema's top-level `$schema` declaration for Claude, closes the child stdin, isolates its cwd, enforces a wall-clock bound, requires `structured_output`, independently validates the canonical verdict and identity, retries malformed output once, and classifies structured HTTP 429 before wording fallbacks.

Return exactly two parts and no surrounding prose: the line `AGENT_GUILD_COURIER_OUTCOME`, then the runner's JSON object unchanged. The Codex return gate validates that object before allowing the read-only handoff. The parent persists it as follows:

- For `status: "verdict"`, write the supplied verdict unchanged to `.agent-guild/state/verdicts/<Task-ID>-<tier>-r<retries>-claude.json`, validate and render it with the Guild-owned helpers, then append the supplied metrics through `ledger-append.py` with lane vendor `claude`, the brief path, and the verified verdict path.
- For `status: "quota"`, append the supplied ledger metrics first with `--quota-event` and no artifacts, then create `.agent-guild/state/exhausted/claude`. Write no verdict.

Missing CLI access, authentication failures, timeouts, and twice-malformed output arrive as a validated `blocked` suffixed verdict plus ledger metrics. They never replace or alter the unsuffixed in-family verdict of record.

## Codex Host: Read-Only Return

This host runs you `sandbox_mode: read-only`. You cannot write your verdict into `.agent-guild/state/verdicts/`, and the return gate does not expect you to.

Compose the verdict exactly as `.agent-guild/schemas/verdict.schema.json` defines it, with `task_id` set to the Task-ID you were dispatched on and `checker` set to your own agent name. Return exactly two parts and no surrounding prose: the line `AGENT_GUILD_VERDICT`, then the JSON object unchanged.

The return gate validates that object against the schema and confirms its identity before letting you finish. The parent then writes it verbatim to `.agent-guild/state/verdicts/<Task-ID>-<tier>-r<retries>.json` and renders the Markdown sibling with the Guild-owned helpers. The parent transcribes your verdict; it does not author one, and it must not edit the object it received.

Everything else about your job is unchanged. Re-derive every claim from the artifacts rather than trusting a worker's self-report.

skill_body_suffixes.init:
## Codex Plugin Command

Resolve `<skill-directory>` to the directory containing this `SKILL.md`, resolve `<project-root>` to the current repository root, then run the shared installer:

```sh
python3 "<skill-directory>/../../project-template/install.py" codex "<project-root>"
```

Do not add `--project-skills` for plugin setup—the installed plugin already supplies them. Codex does not automatically trust plugin hooks: after the installer succeeds, open `/hooks`, review the exact Agent Guild definitions, and ask the user to trust them explicitly. Never imply that installing or initializing the plugin granted trust. Then start existing work with `$agent-guild:job <issue|file|url>` or author a fresh spec with `$agent-guild:constitution`.
